page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration powered by an Intel x86_64 processor. The instance provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache hierarchy details include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 256 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The server includes no GPUs, features no local storage, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware instruction flags include broad acceleration capabilities such as AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 extensions), AMX (tile and int8), AES, and VAES. Benchmark metrics indicate robust multithreaded capacity and memory throughput. The server achieved 17,690.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, a PassMark CPU score of 67,610.19, and 72,759.95 in CPU extended instructions tests, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated 277.75 GB/sec for uncached reads and 122.41 GB/sec for writes. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,777.0 and stress-ng single-core output of 1,689.08, sit in the middle 50% tier.

Operational benchmarks highlight solid data and network processing capability. Redis SET operations reached 70.46 million operations per second, accompanied by a PassMark database score of 30,504.05 and static web serving throughput of 86.82 GB/sec, all registering in the top 25%. While lacking dedicated GPU silicon, matrix acceleration via AMX and vector units enables competitive CPU-based inference, achieving 2,672.73 tokens/sec on prompt processing for 135M parameter models and 33.98 tokens/sec generation on 7B parameter models.

The primary tradeoffs of the n4-standard-64 include its reliance on network-attached storage due to zero bundled local disks, and average single-thread performance compared to higher-frequency compute-oriented instances. Its high density of 64 vCPUs and 256 GB RAM delivers cost-effective resource aggregation for parallelized workloads, in-memory caching systems, distributed build environments, relational databases, and high-concurrency web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs on 32 Intel physical cores and 256 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Built on x86_64 architecture with 260 MB of L3 cache, it integrates advanced execution instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate strong multithreaded performance, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,690.0, a PassMark CPU score of 67,610.19, and uncached read bandwidth of 277.75 GB/sec. Operational metrics excel in Redis SET throughput (70.46 million ops/sec) and static web serving (86.82 GB/sec). While single-core execution sits in the mid-tier, the instance provides dense, balanced resource allocation suitable for enterprise databases, caching layers, software compilation, and parallelized backend web tiers.

256 GB system memory (standard 4 GB per vCPU allocation)
Hardware support for AVX-512, AMX int8/tile, and AES cryptographic instructions
